poem.content:
In the coil of a forgotten memory, a frog sits still
Watching the ocean's waves, his eyes a depthless pool
The awkward peace of autumn's twilight descends, a veil
Shrouding all, in a rime of worn stone and seaweed's petal

A ship sails forth, a solitary voyager, riding tides
_through_ the mirrored library of time, where history resides
In the camp of night, a wife awaits, her face an unread page
Where the hours are measured by the stars, and love's an endless leash

The error of forgotten songs pierces my ear, a reminder of all
The secrets hidden 'neath the surface, beyond the siren's call
My body trembles, warning me to turn away
Yet, I'm drawn to the edge of an unseen cliff, where fears have no shore

As I climb the winding ladder of the past, its rungs a multiplying spoiler
The earth grows old, its memories exploding like stars in flight
Before me, the divide beckons, vast and impermeable as the tree
My nose climbs a muzzle, offering no solace to the owl in flight

Over the ocean's shouldering waves, I whisper secrets to my heart
Till the body language of fish swimming in formation yields
In libraries underground, wisdom prescribed the formulas
Of a loving wife, sweet moth hung suspended in friction's lax focus

Your compass needle wavers, an incomplete ascent towards afternoon
Meanwhile, time slips quietly into the all-convincing trade show closet.
